newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish council calls for easing of emergency rule.
newsitem.headline: Turkish council calls for easing of emergency rule.

text.p: Turkey's influential National Security Council on Thursday recommended that a state of emergency in one of 10 southeastern provinces should be lifted because of a drop in Kurdish rebel activity, Anatolian news agency said.
The military-dominated body said emergency rule should end in the province of Mardin, which has a mixed Arab, Kurdish and Turkish population, at the end of November.
It recommended that emergency rule, a step away from martial law, should continue in nine other provinces, the agency said.
Emergency rule has been in force in much of the southeast since 1987 to combat Kurdistan Workers Party (KDP) rebels fighting for autonomy or independence.
Turkish officials said on Thursday that government forces had killed 25 guerrillas in two days of clashes in which one member of the security forces died.

The rebels died in the southeastern provinces of Diyarbakir, Bingol, Sirnak and Hakkari in fighting on Wednesday and Thursday, the regional governor's office in the city of Diyarbakir said in a statement.
It did not say where the member of the security forces was killed.
Three rebels and eight other people have been killed in two PKK suicide bomb attacks in the past week. More than 21,000 people have died in the 12-year-old conflict.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan was due to visit Mardin on Friday.
